title: Start quiz
intro: Eight jobs, one tool each. Pick Jev, an LLM or plain Code for every job. You will take a matching quiz at the end and see how much you improved.

questions.prompt: A help desk gets 20,000 messages a day, and each one must go to one of six queues. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: One quick judgment repeated at scale is Jev's home ground: a typed Choice per message, fast, and billed only for the tokens it reads.

questions.prompt: A customer asks why their parcel is late. You need a friendly reply written for them. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Writing free text is System Two work. Jev has no question type that holds a sentence, so an LLM writes it.

questions.prompt: For every order, work out exactly how many days passed between the order date and the delivery date. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Date math is exact, and Jev judges rather than calculates. Plain Code gets it right every time, for free.

questions.prompt: You want each answer to come with a number saying how sure it is, so shaky answers can go to a person. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: A Noul from Jev is a probability, so its confidence is built in and can be checked. An LLM's answer is only words.

questions.prompt: Five yes or no judgments about a CV must become one final score, using weights the hiring team can change. Which tool does the combining?
questions.explanation: Jev answers the small questions. Combining them with weights is plain arithmetic, so Code does it and the team can change the weights without asking Jev again.

questions.prompt: Summarize a 30 page contract in plain English for a customer. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Summarizing is open-ended writing. Jev returns typed answers, not prose, and Code has no rule for it.

questions.prompt: Check every incoming email for ten warning signs of phishing, with how likely each sign is. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: One request can carry all ten yes or no questions, and each answer is its own probability. That is cheap and fast.

questions.prompt: Never approve a refund above 500 dollars, whatever the customer's message says. Which tool enforces that rule?
questions.explanation: A hard rule must never bend. Text from outsiders can try to give orders to a model, but a Code check on the number cannot be talked out of it.
